== Biography ==
'''Samuel Glasgow''' was born in Ireland, reportedly on 12 May 1841. He is currently attached as a son of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]] and [[Fee-681|Elizabeth Fee]], but both parent relationships are uncertain and are discussed below.

{{Migrating Ancestor|origin = Ireland|destination = Queensland|origin-flag = European_Flags-29.png|destination-flag = Flags_of_Australian-5.png}}
He migrated to Queensland, Australia as a young man. A published biography of his son states that Samuel came from County Armagh to Queensland in 1863.<ref name="SenateBio">[https://biography.senate.gov.au/glasgow-thomas-william/ Biographical Dictionary of the Australian Senate], Thomas William Glasgow.</ref>

{{Occupation|image=Wikimedia_Commons_photos-3.jpg|text=was engaged in farming}}

He married [[Armstrong-12775|'''Matilda Armstrong''']] in 1864 in Queensland.<ref>[https://www.qld.gov.au/law/births-deaths-marriages-and-divorces/family-history-research Queensland Marriage Index #C416/1864]</ref>  They had one daughter before Matilda tragically died in 1867.

He married [[Anderson-37968|'''Mary Margaret Trotter Anderson''']] in 1869 in Queensland.<ref>[https://www.qld.gov.au/law/births-deaths-marriages-and-divorces/family-history-research Queensland Mariage Index #C288/1869]</ref>  They had a further thirteen children together.  

After Samuel's sons, [[Glasgow-773|Bill]] and [[Glasgow-791|Alexander]], returned from the Boer War, they purchased his grocery store in Gympie and set up a partnership, TW & A Glasgow Ltd.

Mary and Samuel retired to Brisbane where, in 1912, Mary left him a widower for the second time.  Samuel passed away in 1916 at Brisbane.<ref>[https://www.qld.gov.au/law/births-deaths-marriages-and-divorces/family-history-research Queensland Death Index #B23079/1916]</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3140]] is assessed at 58% (possible). The selected John represents the Elizabeth Fee family reconstruction, and Samuel’s independently reported Armagh origin fits that broad setting. No held contemporary record names Samuel’s parents or connects him to the specific Killyreavy John; the profile’s older Antrim attachment and America narrative are unresolved alternatives.

Confidence concerns this recorded child and the selected father as identified by the held family evidence; maternity and the father’s upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Obtain Samuel’s 1916 Queensland death certificate and 1864 marriage with parent fields.

Source basis already held: [https://www.qld.gov.au/law/births-deaths-marriages-and-divorces/family-history-research Queensland Death Index #B23079/1916 (https://www.qld.gov.au/law/births-deaths-marriages-and-divorces/family-history-research)]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



=== Parents ===

No contemporary record cited on this profile names Samuel's parents. His reported County Armagh origin conflicts with identifying his father as [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]], the County Antrim farmer of Lisnagaver who married Margaret Garvin and died in 1895. The existing father and mother relationships are therefore marked uncertain.

[[Glasgow-3140|John Glasgow]] represents the competing family reconstruction in which a John Glasgow married Elizabeth Fee. That profile may itself combine [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]]'s son, who was recorded in America in 1851, with an Armagh family. A widowed farmer named John Glasgow died at Killyreavy, County Armagh, in 1882, and was father of Martha Jane Glasgow, wife of James Campbell.<ref name="KillyreavyDeath">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1883/06378/4830400.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register], John Glasgow, Killyreavy, 27 December 1882.</ref><ref name="CampbellMarriage">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1873/11258/8128996.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], James Campbell and Martha Jane Glasgow, 20 February 1873.</ref> He is a stronger geographic candidate for Samuel's family, but no located record yet names Samuel as his son or Elizabeth Fee as his wife.
